title: Time and space bounds from space-bounded computation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $f$ map binary words to binary words, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input $x$, $M$ halts with output $f(x)$ at some time while using at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells. Then $M$ computes $f$ within time $B(|x|,s(|x|))$, where $B(n,r)=(|Q|+1)(n+2)3^{k(2r+1)}(2r+1)^k$, $k$ is the number of work tapes, and $Q$ is its state set. Moreover, for every binary input $x$ and every time $t$, the computation from the initial configuration on $x$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells.
